title: Establishing and utilizing different physiological three-dimensional cell cultures from carcinomas of the breast for personalized cancer therapy
summary: Cancer therapy should be individualized. This requires laboratory models that reflect the growth conditions in the patient. In an interdisciplinary collaboration between researchers from the Department of Radiation Oncology and Radiation Oncology / OncoRay - National Center for Radiation Research in Oncology of the TU Dresden and colleagues from the clinics for gynecology and obstetrics, Clinic for Plastic, Reconstructive and Breast Surgery and the Institute of Pathology of the Städtischen Klinikum Görlitz, three-dimensional cell cultures will be established, characterized and subsequently used for the development of personalized therapy. Here the therapy response and the development of therapy resistances can be examined and unraveled in detail in tumor stem cells and microtumors close to the patient. This study focuses on carcinomas of the breast for which an optimization and individualization of therapy is urgently required.

interventions.name: Provision of surgical material to establish four distinct 3D cell culture models from tissue of carcinomas of the breast.
